To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the time-dependent profile due to diffusion of the chemical reagent in the solution above a membrane can be neglected in the study of the membrane response after some time, and that the ratio of the change of the spontaneous curvature to the equilibrium density can be obtained from the dynamics of membrane deformation.

the spatiotemporally resolved dynamics of the response of a lipid vesicle submitted to a chemical modification of the environment above the membrane can be used to determine the spontaneous curvature and the friction between the monolayers of the membrane.

the membrane response to a local chemical modification is dominated by intermonolayers friction, and that the ratio between the spontaneous curvature change and the equilibrium density change can be extracted from a spatiotemporally resolved measurement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of a lipid membrane that is locally perturbed.
the dynamics of a lipid bilayer membrane submitted to a spatially varying local chemical modification.
the study of the spatiotemporally resolved response of a membrane to a local chemical modification of its environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spatiotemporally resolved membrane response to a local chemical modification provides a powerful tool to probe the membrane properties.
the membrane response to a local chemical modification is governed by a competition between the intermonolayer and the monolayer friction.
the spatiotemproal response of a vesicle to a local chemical modification can be used to determine the membrane properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spatiotemporally resolved dynamics of a vesicle submitted to local chemical modifications can be used to extract the properties of a lipid membrane, which cannot be obtained by other means.
the time-dependent response of a lipid vesicle to a local chemical inhomogeneity can be used as a tool to extract information on the membrane properties.
the spatiotemporally resolved response of a lipid bilayer membrane to a local chemical perturbation provides a unique tool to extract its mechanical properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of the spatiotemporally resolved membrane deformation can be used to extract information on the mechanical response of membranes.
the dynamics of the membrane deformation can be used as a tool to probe the mechanical properties of the membrane.
the dynamics of a membrane response to a local chemical inhomogeneity is a powerful tool to characterize the properties of the membrane.
